expected_evidence: geological: platinum (and possibly iridium/osmium) enrichment layer at the ~12,900 cal BP Younger Dryas onset horizon in Greenland ice cores (e.g., GISP2, NEEM), synchronous with known YD boundary layer (YDB) sediments elsewhere
material: microspherules, meltglass, nanodiamonds, magnetic/carbon spherules in the same ice or associated terrestrial YDB sedimentary sequences
geological/material: elevated soot, charcoal, and combustion aerosol markers (biomass-burning proxy) in the ice matching an 'impact winter' signature
astronomical: independent lines of evidence for an extraterrestrial body (comet/asteroid fragment) such as cosmic dust/micrometeorite flux anomalies, or (weakly) a candidate crater/airburst structure
genetic: coincident megafaunal extinction/population bottleneck signals and possibly human population contraction in the relevant interval
model_prior: existing YDIH literature (Firestone et al. 2007; Petaev et al. 2013 platinum spike paper; subsequent replication attempts and critiques) documenting this exact claim

oral_tradition/iconographic: highly speculative cometary imagery (e.g., claimed Göbekli Tepe 'vulture stone') or flood/fire myths sometimes invoked by proponents, though these are contested and low-confidence
textual: none expected, as this predates writing entirely
response.rationale: The interval -10950 corresponds to ~12,900 cal BP, the Younger Dryas onset, so the younger-dryas detectability row is the appropriate reference rather than a blended/unspecified default. Ice-core geochemistry (geological, 0.65) and astronomical/cosmic-dust proxies (0.7) are the highest-detectability channels here, and this is exactly the type of evidence actually reported in the literature: a platinum anomaly at the YD boundary in Greenland ice (model-prior, unverified against the provided evidence text: Petaev et al. 2013 and related YDIH work; this is drawn from training recall, not the task's evidence corpus, so flagged as model-prior). Material markers like spherules/nanodiamonds/soot (0.35) are moderately detectable and have been claimed in terrestrial YDB sites, though replication has been contentious. Genetic (0.3), linguistic (0.05), oral_tradition (0.1), and iconographic (0.1) are all low-detectability for this pre-literate, deep-time interval, and textual evidence is impossible (0.0) since writing did not yet exist. Given that the core physical/geochemical evidence types (geological, astronomical, material) sit in the 0.35β0.7 range, absence of corroborating textual/oral/iconographic evidence should not be read as evidence against the hypothesis β it is expected under this detectability profile. The suggested aggregate adjustment of 0.6 reflects that the hypothesis's most diagnostic evidence types (ice-core geochemistry, cosmic proxies) are reasonably preservable and searchable, making a genuine test of the hypothesis plausible, while acknowledging that confirmation remains empirically contested in the broader (recalled, not sourced-here) literature.
